meta.note: Plain-language explanations for readers who are new to the terms. They are summaries, not the legal definitions: the instrument named under 'See' governs.

terms.def: A centre set up under the SEZ Act that deals with non-residents and in foreign currency much as an offshore centre would, while sitting inside India. GIFT IFSC in Gujarat is the operational one.
The single regulator for banking, capital markets, funds and insurance in an IFSC. It exercises the powers RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA would otherwise have there.

terms.term: Unit in an IFSC as a non-resident
terms.def: Under the FEMA (IFSC) Regulations, a financial institution or branch set up in an IFSC is treated as a person resident outside India, so dealings with Indian residents are cross-border for FEMA.
A branch of an Indian or foreign bank set up in an IFSC. It keeps USD 20 million of capital at the parent bank level.
A bank set up as a subsidiary company in an IFSC, with minimum capital of USD 50 million.
A currency listed in the First Schedule to the Banking Regulations in which Banking Units may do business, such as USD, EUR, GBP, JPY and, since 2024, SEK, NOK, NZD and DKK.
The regulator of the parent entity in its home country. Branches in the IFSC often follow the home regulator's prudential norms, for example on leverage or solvency.
High-quality liquid assets as a share of net cash outflows over 30 days of stress. IBUs keep 100% or the home regulator's minimum where higher.
A company (subsidiary, joint venture or new company) registered with IFSCA to carry on lending, leasing, treasury or other permitted finance activities in the IFSC.
A branch in the IFSC of a company incorporated in India or abroad, registered to carry on finance activities.
For finance companies: lending, factoring and forfaiting, investments, derivatives and global or regional corporate treasury centres. These attract capital, liquidity and exposure norms.
For finance companies: services such as merchant banking, investment advice, operating leases of aircraft and ships, distribution and similar activities, kept in a separate department.

The capital a finance company must hold: for example USD 3 million for core activities (including financial leasing) and USD 0.2 million for a treasury centre or an operating lessor of aircraft or ships.
A finance company or unit in the IFSC that runs treasury functions for its group entities.
A finance company or unit registered to buy trade receivables, with or without recourse, and to register assignments with the Central Registry.
An entity registered with IFSCA to manage funds and portfolios in the IFSC: an Authorised FME, a Registered FME (Non-Retail) or a Registered FME (Retail).
A fund scheme offered by private placement to accredited or high-value investors (minimum USD 150,000), similar in function to an alternative investment fund.
A fund scheme offered to the public, with at least 20 investors and a USD 3 million corpus, managed only by a Registered FME (Retail).
A scheme investing in start-ups and early-stage companies, managed by an Authorised FME, with a corpus of USD 3 million to USD 200 million.
A fund that pools the money of a single family, with a minimum corpus of USD 10 million.
An investor recognised as financially sophisticated, who may invest below the usual minimum ticket size in venture capital and restricted schemes.
The principal officer, compliance officer and other key staff of a regulated entity. FME and CMI rules require them to be based in the IFSC.

A broker dealer, clearing member, credit rating agency, custodian, debenture trustee, depository participant, distributor, investment adviser, investment banker or similar entity registered under the CMI Regulations.
A single registration through the Single Window IT System covering several capital market activities, with a fee for each activity.
The online system through which applications for IFSC registrations, SEZ approvals and related clearances are filed.
A branch or company of an insurer or reinsurer registered with IFSCA to write life, general, health or reinsurance business in the IFSC.
A broker, corporate agent, third-party administrator, surveyor or web aggregator registered to act in the IFSC.
An agent that underwrites and binds insurance from the IFSC on behalf of a foreign insurer under a binding authority agreement. It keeps USD 500,000 of capital with an IBU.
The capital an insurer allocates to its IFSC branch, at least USD 1.5 million.
Available solvency margin as a share of the required margin. IIOs writing general, health or reinsurance business keep at least 150%.
A rupee account an IFSC unit may hold with an AD bank in India for its business outside the IFSC. Receipts are moved to its IBU account in foreign currency within 30 working days.
The director responsible for the entity's AML compliance. With the Principal Officer, they must hold the NISM-IFSCA-01 certification.
FIU-IND's portal on which IFSC entities file cash, suspicious and other reports under the PML Rules.
The officer, at or one level below KMP, who hears a customer's appeal against the entity's decision on a complaint.
The approval under the SEZ Act that every IFSC unit needs to operate in the zone, renewed before expiry.
The national agency for cyber incidents. IFSC entities follow its advisories and use auditors it empanels.
